name: AeroFusion — Scene 0 → Scene 1: the ember becomes a Punjab field fire
note: One unbroken camera move. Frame i corresponds to t = i / (frames - 1). Every frame is a pure function of t, so the sequence can be re-rendered at any frame count or resolution with render/frames.py and stays identical in motion. v2: rice-stubble clumps with loose straw, rounded flickering flames, C1-continuous camera path (no stops between keyframes), 360 frames.

files.png_sequence: render with render/frames.py (lossless, for After Effects / DaVinci / Premiere)

phases.camera: macro, locked on the ember, dark background
phases.what_happens: A single matte orange ember floats in darkness and pulses gently.
The ember flashes and bursts into ~320 sparks; the core shrinks into one hot spark.
phases.suggested_copy: Thirty times thinner than a human hair.

phases.camera: follows the spark down, tilting to look at the ground
phases.what_happens: The spark drifts down on the wind; dark stubble appears, lit only by the spark.
The spark lands; the straw catches; the first flames and smoke appear.

phases.camera: rises overhead (keeps the plume out of the lens), then swings to the drone view
phases.what_happens: The fire line spreads across the field, the burnt patch grows, smoke plumes rise and flatten under the ceiling, and the dusk world fades in from darkness: fields, tree lines, tube-well hut, tractor, village, other fires on the horizon.
phases.suggested_copy: A farmer has two weeks between rice and wheat. Fire is the fastest way to clear the field.

phases.what_happens: Final composition; matches the standalone Scene 1 still.
phases.suggested_copy: NASA's satellite saw this fire from 830 km up.

style.look: stylized toy 3D: rounded clay-like shapes, cotton-ball trees, lumpy irregular smoke, violet-magenta dusk, warm practical lights, bloom, fine film grain
